Robot Doctor Code & OpModes

Robot won't stop when I press STOP

Keeps running, "stuck in stop", or the app restarts. Below are the 2 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 1 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • Is there a while loop that doesn't check opModeIsActive(), or a sleep/loop inside an iterative loop()? Search for "while (" and check every loop.

Common causes and how to fix them

1 A loop that ignores STOP

A while loop without opModeIsActive() keeps running after STOP. The SDK gives up after a few seconds ("stuck in stop") and restarts the app.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. Every while loop in a LinearOpMode must include opModeIsActive() (or !isStopRequested() before start).
  2. In an iterative OpMode, never loop or sleep inside loop(). It must return quickly, every time.
  3. Long threads you start yourself must also check for stop.
Cooperative loop
while (opModeIsActive() && !touch.isPressed()) {
    // keep driving until the sensor is pressed or STOP is hit
}

Sources: FTC Docs · Troubleshooting common issues · GM0 · Common software issues

2 Your code is blocking the robot controller

A long loop or sleep can make the robot look disconnected: ping climbs and the controls stop responding even though Wi-Fi is fine.

How to fix it 15 min

  1. Check whether the problem only happens in one OpMode. An empty OpMode with good ping means the link is fine and the code is the issue.
  2. Never sleep or loop for a long time inside an iterative OpMode's loop(). Use a timer and check it each loop instead.
  3. In LinearOpMode, every while loop must check opModeIsActive().

Sources: FTC Docs · Wireless issues at events · GM0 · Common software issues
